newsitem.title: UK: Copper may top 95 cents a pound soon - Macquarie.
newsitem.headline: Copper may top 95 cents a pound soon - Macquarie.

text.p: Copper prices may rise above 95 cents a pound ($2,094/tonne) soon as the possibility of another squeeze develops, Macquarie Equities said in their latest weekly commodities report.
"The still lower level of stocks, coupled with continued strong demand for physical material from China, holds out the possibility of a further "mini-squeeze' developing," Macquarie said.
"We think prices could break above 90 cents a pound ($1,984/tonne) in the coming weeks and even breach 95 cents."
Macquarie also said traders may try to force prices above $2,000 in the run-up to the October options expiry on Wednesday.

In 1996 the copper market looks increasingly likely to be in balance or even showing a small deficit after allowing for 80,000 tonnes of copper that has apparently gone back into the Chinese strategic stockpile, Macquarie's report said. But prices are down because Sumitomo Corp's former trader Yasuo Hamanaka kept prices artificially high by withholding stocks, and because of the overhang of around one million tonnes of Sumitomo longs "yet to be liquidated," it added.

Macquarie said there has been a 300,000-tonne build-up of copper concentrates in 1995/96, partly at RTZ-CRA's Kennecott smelter -- "holding out the prospect of a large rise in refined output in 1997."
